title: TLS certificate verification disabled in four scrapers
severity_rationale: Integrity risk to collected data; no credentials travel over the affected connections; fix can change what the scrapers can reach
location: scrapers/brazil/tjrj_scraper.py:16-17; scrapers/netherlands/rechtspraak_district_courts.py:18-19; scrapers/netherlands/rechtspraak_expanded.py:12-13; scrapers/netherlands/rechtspraak_scraper.py:20-21
evidence: Each file builds an SSL context with check_hostname=False and verify_mode=ssl.CERT_NONE, so server certificates are not validated. The four CanLII/LDH scrapers do not do this.
why_it_matters: A network intermediary could alter what is recorded as a court decision without the scraper noticing. The Dutch endpoints are public and normally present valid certificates, so verification is probably unnecessary to disable there; the README records a TLS error for TJCE, so the Brazilian case may have been a workaround.
recommended_correction: Use the default verified context; if a particular Brazilian host has a broken chain, pin that host with its own CA bundle and record the exception here. Re-collect or re-verify a sample afterwards.
verification: tests/test_repository_hygiene.py::TestKnownScraperDefects.test_f_tls_verification_is_not_disabled (expected failure today; passes when fixed). Not run against any live site.
uncertainty: Not known whether the original collection hit certificate errors. Changing this could make some scrapers stop working, so it changes data-collection behaviour.
researcher_decision_needed: yes: approve the change and say whether TJRJ needs a pinned CA

title: Seven scrapers imitate a browser; one gives a placeholder contact
severity_rationale: Transparency and terms-of-use posture of data collection; no effect on data content
location: User-Agent set to a desktop-browser string: scrapers/brazil/tjrj_scraper.py:24, tjac_scraper.py:17, tjpi_scraper.py:16, tjsc_scraper.py:15, tjrr_scraper.py:15, tjdft_scraper.py:11, tjto_scraper.py:20. Placeholder contact address in scrapers/netherlands/rechtspraak_scraper.py:22
evidence: Seven Brazilian scrapers present themselves as Chrome on Windows. The Canadian scrapers and two Dutch scrapers identify the project and its repository; rechtspraak_scraper.py names a placeholder contact (your-email@example.com).
why_it_matters: A scraper that imitates a browser cannot be identified or contacted by the court operating the site, which is at odds with the transparent-conduct posture of the rest of the project, and a placeholder contact gives a site operator nobody to reach.
recommended_correction: Identify the project honestly (project name, repository URL, a monitored contact address) in every scraper. Some ESAJ hosts may reject non-browser agents; if so, record that outcome rather than disguising the client.
verification: tests/test_repository_hygiene.py::test_f_user_agent_does_not_imitate_a_browser and ::test_f_user_agent_has_no_placeholder_contact (expected failures today).
uncertainty: Not known whether the Brazilian hosts would serve the same content to an identified client; that would need a controlled live test, which was not done.
researcher_decision_needed: yes: choose the contact address; approve a controlled test

title: Licensed database exports committed to a public repository
severity_rationale: Possibly irreversible once public; licence terms were not read in this audit and may or may not forbid redistribution; this is not a legal opinion
location: legal-last-mile-systematic-review/01_search/raw_exports/ (about 124 MB: 19 Scopus, 1 Web of Science, 1 HeinOnline, 2 ProQuest, 1 JSTOR export files plus native/ copies); 01_search/deduplicated/deduplicated_records.csv
evidence: Database exports (bibliographic records with abstracts, as downloaded) from subscription databases are tracked in the public repository. The repository README says full-text PDFs are withheld for licensing reasons; the same question has not been recorded for the database exports.
why_it_matters: Subscription databases usually license export for the subscriber's own research use; whether bulk redistribution of exported records is allowed varies by database and contract. A takedown request or breach finding would fall on the author and the institution.
recommended_correction: Read each database's export/redistribution terms (with the EUR library). If redistribution is not clearly allowed, replace the exports in the working tree by their record IDs and SHA-256 (already in 10_reproducibility/DATA_MANIFEST.csv) and keep the files privately. Removing them from Git history is a separate, deliberate decision that was not taken.
verification: Counted and sized; terms not retrieved (no live requests were made).
uncertainty: The terms could well permit this. Unknown until read.
researcher_decision_needed: yes: decide after reading the terms

title: Win/loss patterns code "indevido" phrases in the wrong direction
severity_rationale: Affects a headline analytic variable (who wins) for the Brazilian sub-dataset; size of the effect cannot be measured because the coded dataset is not in the repository
location: utils/jurimetric_coding.py:581-583 (user-wins patterns) and :605-607 (utility-wins patterns)
evidence: The pattern \bcorte.*?indevid\b requires the word to END at "indevid", so it never matches "indevido"; at the same time \bcorte.*?devido\b matches the "devido" inside "indevido". Offline probes (tests/test_offline_helpers.py): "corte indevido do fornecimento de água" is coded utility_wins and "suspensão indevida do fornecimento de água" is coded mixed, where user_wins is the evident intent. Both are recorded as expected failures.
why_it_matters: Unlawful-disconnection claims are a central kind of Brazilian water dispute; if they are coded in the opposite direction, outcome statistics for Brazil are biased in an unknown direction and degree.
recommended_correction: Anchor the "devid-" patterns with a leading word boundary and negative look-behind for "in", complete truncated stems, re-run the coding on the full dataset and report the change. This is a change to coded results, so it must not be applied silently.
verification: tests/test_offline_helpers.py::test_improper_disconnection_should_favour_the_user and ::test_improper_suspension_should_favour_the_user (expected failures today).
uncertainty: Prevalence in the real data unknown. The 91-decision validation sample may not include these patterns (outcome coding was not part of the validation described in validation/README.md).
researcher_decision_needed: yes: approve fix and re-coding; decide how to report the change

title: "Absorbed before litigation" asserted from a classifier share
severity_rationale: Interpretation stronger than the data can carry, in the project's headline narrative
location: RESEARCH_CONTEXT.md:55; README.md ("Known Limitations", Netherlands paragraph, line 243); validation/README.md:33
evidence: RESEARCH_CONTEXT.md says 98.56% of Dutch cases "were absorbed before litigation". wiki_key_findings.md:95 shows that 98.56% is the share the v0.3.0 vocabulary filter classified not_water_related (67,665 of 68,654). The README (line 243) calls the related inference "inferential" but still writes that the near-zero connection-refusal count "tells us" the Awb absorbs disputes.

title: Packaging: license string vs declared minimum setuptools

severity_rationale: Possible breach of publisher or database terms and of institutional AI guidance, and loss of control of unpublished work; severity assumes the terms forbid it, which was not verified

title: CITATION.cff files failed schema validation
severity_rationale: The "Cite this repository" metadata could not be read by tools that validate it; trivial to fix
location: CITATION.cff (pre-audit line 18) and legal-last-mile-systematic-review/CITATION.cff (pre-audit line 29)
evidence: Both files carried orcid: "" (an empty string). The Citation File Format 1.2.0 schema requires an ORCID URL, so validation with cffconvert failed on both files.
why_it_matters: GitHub and Zenodo build citations from this file; an invalid file can make that feature fail.
recommended_correction: Leave the key out until the researcher supplies an ORCID.
fixed_in_this_audit: yes: the empty orcid line was removed from both files; no other field was changed.
verification: cffconvert --validate reported the schema error before the change and "Citation metadata are valid according to schema version 1.2.0" for both files after it (scratch virtual environment; not committed). The review verifier still passes (206 checks).
uncertainty: The ORCID, if any, is the researcher's to supply.
researcher_decision_needed: yes: supply an ORCID if one exists

title: TJSP scraper absent; hand-coded set unprovenanced
severity_rationale: Part of the headline dataset cannot be re-collected or traced from the repository; rights in one component are unstated
location: README.md (Brazilian courts table: TJSP 574 cases "ESAJ POST", TJSP 1997-2015 200 cases "hand-coded historical"); scrapers/brazil/ (no TJSP scraper); scrapers/brazil/tjsp_transformation_loader.py:1-17
evidence: No script in scrapers/brazil/ collects TJSP decisions by ESAJ POST, yet the README counts 574 as collected that way. The 200 historical TJSP cases come from a hand-coded 2021 spreadsheet (TJSP-All Cases-transformation-2021.xlsx) that is not in the repository; the repository does not say who coded it, when, or on what terms it may be reused.
why_it_matters: Together 774 of the 11,724 Brazilian decisions (6.6%) have no reproducible route from the repository, and the reuse rights of the hand-coded set are unknown.
recommended_correction: Add the TJSP script (or state that it was lost), and document the origin, author and permission for the 2021 spreadsheet.
verification: Directory listing and file reads.
uncertainty: The script may exist on the researcher's machine.

title: README maps scripts to Dutch subsets inconsistently
severity_rationale: Documentation of which script produced which subset is unreliable; counts cannot be tied to scripts
location: README.md ("Repository Structure" tree and "Netherlands total" paragraph) versus scrapers/netherlands/rechtspraak_scraper.py:1-10, rechtspraak_expanded.py:1-5, rechtspraak_district_courts.py:1-10
evidence: The README attributes the 17,783 Dutch district-court decisions to rechtspraak_scraper.py, but that script's own header enumerates the Raad van State and the CBb; the district courts are handled by rechtspraak_district_courts.py, which the README tree does not list. canada_superior_expanded.py is not in the tree either.
why_it_matters: A reader following the README would run the wrong script for a subset.
recommended_correction: Update the tree and the paragraph to match the scripts.
verification: Headers read; counts not recomputed (data not available).
uncertainty: The README may describe an earlier arrangement of the scripts.
